overview: IT project managers plan and lead technology projects such as new software, cloud moves and system upgrades. They set budgets and schedules, track milestones, solve problems with the team and keep business leaders informed. O*NET rates knowledge of computers and electronics at 4.19 out of 5 for this job and administration at 4. Paths vary: 38% hold a bachelor's degree, 24% an associate degree and 19% a post-baccalaureate certificate. BLS reports pay for a broader computer occupations group, with a median of $116,580. Tight deadlines and conflicts between teams are part of the job.
pay: BLS reports pay for the broader “Computer Occupations, All Other” group, which includes IT project managers. Its median is $116,580, and the top 10% earn $188,470 or more. The District of Columbia pays the most at $156,590, 34% above the national figure. California has 80,150 of these jobs.

faq.q: How much do IT project managers make?
faq.a: BLS reports pay for the broader computer occupations group: a May 2025 median of $116,580. The middle half earn between $79,370 and $157,500. The District of Columbia, Maryland ($144,680) and Colorado ($139,580) have the highest state medians, while Louisiana and Tennessee pay the least.

faq.q: What qualifications do IT project managers need?
faq.a: Most have a bachelor's degree in computer science or information systems, plus years of hands-on IT work. In O*NET data, 38% hold a bachelor's degree and 10% a master's degree. Project management certifications are common, and there are 12 related majors.

faq.q: What does an IT project manager do every day?
faq.a: Most days involve status meetings, tracking tasks and deliverables, managing risks and updating stakeholders. O*NET rates critical thinking at 4.12 out of 5 and writing at 4, since clear plans and reports keep projects on track. Achievement orientation stands out as a work style.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to IT project manager?
faq.a: The closest are Project Management Specialists (96% match), Computer and Information Systems Managers (93%) and Management Analysts (90%), based on O*NET 31.0. Computer and Information Systems Managers earn a median of $175,140 and are a common next step.
